claim_boundary.supports: Own re-derivation (lean4/PregenConstructive.lean, structural recursion) over a list of histories with DecidableEq reports: first-match reconstruction recon returns every listed answer iff the answer is constant on report fibers among the listed histories; recon is none exactly on unreported values; any f returning the listed answers agrees with recon on listed reports; a complete listing plus global fiber constancy gives the factor through the report image (the choice-free bridge to node 163); with an unlisted history of a listed report and a different answer, recon returns the listed answer, which is then wrong. The kernel reports NO axioms at all for the seven general theorems recon_of_fiberConstant, fiberConstantOn_of_recon, listed_history_report_criterion, recon_eq_none_iff, recon_unique, recon_wrong_off_list and listed_factor_exists (relative to the supplied DecidableEq instance on reports); the instance anchors report at most propext (instance_wrong_off_list and instance_not_fiberConstant: propext); the variant for a report type without decidable equality (instance from Classical.propDecidable) reports propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound for that proof term. The external ListedHistorySummary.lean is not in this repository and was not part of the gated evidence; all kernel claims are for the in-repo re-derivation PregenConstructive. Exhaustive native check over ALL listings of length <= ell (repeats included), all reports and all answers for 11 non-degenerate tuples (p >= 1, v >= 1, s >= 1) and 4 degenerate boundary tuples (p = 0, or v = 0 or s = 0, where there is at most one triple): recon correct on every listed history iff listed fiber constant, zero mismatches; complete listings agree with the global criterion; partial_false_positive = triples on a non-complete listing that are listed-fiber-constant but not globally fiber-constant; unlisted_refused/correct/wrong = quadruples (listing, report, answer, unlisted history) whose triple is listed-fiber-constant, classified by what recon returns for the unlisted history.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: Report types without decidable equality (only the classical instance is covered, its proof term uses Classical.choice, and necessity of choice there is not shown); infinite or unlisted populations beyond the explicit complete-listing hypothesis; the unconditional factorization for an arbitrary history type (node PG-HISTORY-REPORT-CRITERION); the external ListedHistorySummary.lean (not in this repository); any probability, measurement or physical reading of reports.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: Over an explicit listing with decidable report equality, first-match reconstruction returns every listed answer iff the answer is constant on the listed report fibers, with no axiom in the kernel for the seven general theorems (relative to the supplied DecidableEq instance on reports); off the listing it refuses unreported values and can be wrong on unlisted histories; verified exhaustively on 11 non-degenerate small tuples.
claim_boundary.next_test: Decide whether the listed criterion survives a report type without decidable equality by a choice-free substitute for the first-match search, or show that the Classical.propDecidable instance is unavoidable there (a choice-free model or an independence argument).

second_review.reviewer: fresh-context same-model reviewer (Claude Sonnet 5.5), final pass, separate from the author, not human-independent
second_review.notes: Cold read of the final run (profile, candidate, check_candidate.py, semantic_mutants.py, p2/p4 host_check, p2/native/lean.stdout.log), lean4/PregenConstructive.lean (sha256 6b600af8 identical to p1/construction) and the DAG node, before the earlier pass. Statement fidelity: recon_of_fiberConstant, fiberConstantOn_of_recon and the iff listed_history_report_criterion say exactly 'first-match returns every listed answer iff the answer is constant on listed report fibres'; recon_eq_none_iff is 'none iff no listed history reports x'; recon_unique is 'any f returning the listed answers agrees with recon on listed reports'; recon_wrong_off_list is conditional on a listed fibre-constant answer, a listed h0, and a differing answer on h with the same report; listed_factor_exists needs a complete listing (forall h, h in hs) and global fibre constancy and returns an existential (a Prop-level factor, built with Option.get, no choice). The p2 lean.stdout.log literally reports 'does not depend on any axioms' for exactly the seven general theorems named in the claim, propext only for instance_not_fiberConstant and instance_wrong_off_list, and propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound for the classical variant, so the axiom sentences in supports and narrowest_claim are exact, including the qualification 'relative to the supplied DecidableEq instance'. Earlier-pass amendments: (a) all applied: the sentence that the external ListedHistorySummary.lean was compiled is gone and replaced by 'not in this repository and not part of the gated evidence'; the tuple count is 11 non-degenerate plus 4 degenerate (I counted the public cases: (0,2,0,0), (0,2,2,2), (2,2,2,0), (2,2,0,2) are the degenerate ones); unlisted_* columns are defined as quadruples over listed-fibre-constant triples; narrowest_claim limits 'no axiom' to the seven general theorems; composition_tree has only first_match_recon; the first-occurrence reduction is stated as a checker-level reduction; classical_instance_axiom_bill replaces the 'costs choice' relation; does_not_support names necessity of choice; the 'listing of full length is complete' near miss exists (semantic_full_length_listing_is_complete). (b) No weakening in the rebuild: the checker enumerates first-occurrence sequences with weights sum_k S2(k,t), builds a first-occurrence table per report, tests listed fibre constancy by pairwise equality, and recomputes global fibre constancy for complete listings; it also asserts the totals sum_{k<=ell} p^k and lists*v^p*s^p. The identity mismatch = 0 / complete_mismatch = 0 is NOT assumed: mismatch is computed as (pair_ok != recon_ok) and compared with the producer value, so a false theorem would be caught. Degenerate tuples (v = 0, s = 0, p = 0) are handled (empty product gives zero triples, the total identity still holds). All 422 coordinate and 8 semantic mutants are rejected; the semantic ones are real counterexamples to the stated bridges (first match always right, partial listing implies global, off-listing never wrong/never refused, repeats ignored, full-length listing complete). (c) Not recorded by the earlier pass: (i) the checker's reduction 'recon depends only on the first-occurrence sequence, weighted by Stirling numbers' is a checker algorithm that no Lean statement supports; it is validated only by agreement with the producer's direct enumeration of all listings (and the exact total identity), which is adequate evidence for the 15 tuples but is not a theorem; the operad text now admits it. (ii) The DAG node's Lean references and its quoted anchor name (fiberConstant_of_recon) point to the external ListedHistorySummary.lean; the in-repo anchor is the re-derivation PregenConstructive with a different name (fiberConstantOn_of_recon) and a re-proved argument. A pinned copy of the external file is staged under inputs/, but no gate compiles it, so the run supports PROVED_LEAN for the re-derivation only. (iii) 'Constructive' is relative: the theorems quantify over a supplied DecidableEq instance on reports; for a general report type that instance is exactly what is not available choice-free, and this is the stated next_test, so the node's headline word 'constructive' should carry that qualifier in the DAG text. (iv) The native census is small (p <= 4, v <= 3, s <= 3, ell <= 4); the claim says 'verified exhaustively on 11 non-degenerate small tuples', which is accurate. next_test (choice-free substitute or unavoidability of Classical.propDecidable) is this node's own obligation and differs from does_not_support (which lists the open condition, not the test).

earlier_pass.notes: Cold read of specsB/PG-PREGEN-CONSTRUCTIVE-SUMMARY.json, pregen_constructive_{check,format,semantic,spec}.py, lean4/PregenConstructive.lean, pfp_pregen_constructive.py, its test, the Rust module, operads/pg_pregen_constructive_summary.yaml and the DAG node. I compiled PregenConstructive (exit 0): recon_of_fiberConstant, fiberConstantOn_of_recon, listed_history_report_criterion, recon_eq_none_iff, recon_unique, recon_wrong_off_list and listed_factor_exists report no axioms; the classical variant reports propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; instance_not_fiberConstant and instance_wrong_off_list report propext (instance_wrong_off_list is an anchor, so 'no axiom in the kernel' in narrowest_claim must be limited to the seven general theorems). The Lean statements say what supports says: the iff, the none-iff-unreported rule, uniqueness on listed reports, wrongness off the listing (conditional on a differing unlisted answer, with the Nat instance as witness), and the complete-listing factor. The checker is the strongest part: it never runs recon on a listing; it enumerates first-occurrence sequences weighted by sum_k S2(k,t), uses a first-occurrence table for recon and pairwise equality for fibre constancy, and also asserts the weight totals sum_{k<=ell} p^k and lists*v^p*s^p. I verified the weight for p=0 and the (3,3,2,2) list count 40 and the duplicate-free count 16 used by a mutant. Problems: (1) supports claims the external ListedHistorySummary.lean 'was also compiled and reports no axioms for its eight anchors', but that file is not in the repository (glob finds none), is not pinned by sha256, and is not a p2 gate; the same applies to every line number cited from it (37, 116, 132, 152, 188, 205, 241-254). The DAG node's own Lean refs are to that external file, so this run supports PROVED_LEAN only for the in-repo re-derivation. (2) '15 small tuples' includes four degenerate ones: (0,2,0,0) and (0,2,2,2) have p = 0 (a single empty triple) and (2,2,2,0), (2,2,0,2) have zero triples, so only 11 tuples check anything. (3) the unlisted_refused/correct/wrong counts are quadruples (listing, report, answer, unlisted history) restricted to listed-fibre-constant triples, which the profile does not say. (4) composition_tree contains image_factor_from_listing(first_match_recon(...)), which failed_compositions rejects for a colour mismatch. (5) the checked composition first_match_recon o listing asserts 'only the order of first occurrences matters', which has no Lean anchor and is not what its licensing relation recon_unique states; it is the checker's algorithmic assumption (validated only by producer/checker agreement). (6) the relation classical_instance_costs_choice reads as if choice were necessary; the evidence is only that this proof term uses it; necessity is the open next_test. Mutants are real counterexamples to stated bridges, but a key hypothesis of listed_factor_exists, completeness, has no near miss. next_test is this node's own unpaid obligation and differs from does_not_support.
